text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered for p50-api-latency spike in production (us-west-2). Spike originated on /v1/generate. Initial alert: sustained p95 > 2s and backend queue length growing.

maria (oncall): I'm paged, looking. @derek can you pull the runtime dashboards and worker queue depths?

derek: Looking now. gpu-pool gen-usw2-1 showing 95-100% utilization across serving pods. Continuous-batching backlog rising from ~2k -> 14k in 12m, per-worker inflight queue length 120 -> 420. No clear 5xx spike besides a few 503s from overloaded frontends.

alex: Noticed a change in request distribution — a few keys are emitting sustained high small-req traffic causing many tiny batches. We can trade latency for throughput by bumping batch window. Recommend increasing max_batch_latency_ms from 20 -> 100 and max_batch_size 64 -> 256 for rdx-43b on /v1/generate. Throughput should improve and 503s reduce, p50 up by ~40-80ms.

maria (oncall): Sounds reasonable. Scope? global effect or targeted to problematic model/route? We want to avoid hurting latency-sensitive customers.

alex: Target the model route used by most noisy traffic: model_id=rdx-43b, route=/v1/generate. Also enable "throughput-priority" dynamic batching so the runtime favors larger batches within the window. We'll keep per-customer soft QPS caps in parallel.

derek: I'll also set a temporary route-level rate limit for anonymous API keys to cut down noise: anonymous -> 200/min (was 400/min). That should reduce small-request spam.

maria (oncall): Execute plan. Post commands here and confirm when applied. Also notify CS for customers experiencing timeouts.

alex: Applying runtime config now:
```bash
# increase batching window + batch size for rdx-43b on gen route
redwoodctl runtime update --pool gen-usw2-1 --model rdx-43b --route /v1/generate \
  --set max_batch_latency_ms=100 --set max_batch_size=256 --set batching_strategy=throughput-priority
```

deploy-bot: config change scheduled: runtime-update/1769154321 queued -> applying to pool gen-usw2-1 in 30s. Change will roll to 3 pods with 10s drain between pods.

alex: Rolled to first pod. Observing queue behavior: batch sizes jumped avg 6 -> 42, CPU/GPU utilization stays high but throughput increased ~1.9x on that pod. p50 latency increased ~55ms, p95 dropped from 2.8s -> 1.9s on that pod. No new 5xx from that node.

derek: Rate-limit change for anonymous keys:
```bash
redwoodctl ratelimit set --route /v1/generate --key_type anonymous --limit 200/m --scope global --note "mitigation - reduce small-request noise"
```

deploy-bot: ratelimit update applied; policy active in 10s.

maria (oncall): Early customer impact check: traffic noise reduced, overall p95 improved cluster-wide from 2.7s -> 1.6s. A handful of enterprise customers reported timeouts in the last 15m (customer-A). CS on it.

jen: I reached out to CS and SE. Notified Customer-A: brief note that we're mitigating a platform performance event and we've applied throughput-optimized batching; offered temporary burst capacity if they need lower-latency service while we stabilize.

alex: Monitoring notes: keep an eye on request tail latency for low-tier keys (they might see more noticeable latency bump). For high-tier enterprise keys we can keep per-key overrides to preserve low max_batch_latency_ms.

maria (oncall): Good point. Let's add an explicit override for enterprise keys to keep max_batch_latency_ms=20. Command:
```bash
redwoodctl runtime update --pool gen-usw2-1 --model rdx-43b --route /v1/generate \
  --set-by-key customer_tier=enterprise:max_batch_latency_ms=20
```

alex: Adding override now. Applied. Enterprise traffic remains at low latency on first observations.

incident-bot: Incident severity set to SEV2. Incident channel: #inc-1769154321. Pager cleared for oncall?

maria (oncall): Pager moving to monitoring state. Still in incident. Key actions performed: 1) increased batching window to 100ms and batch_size to 256 for model rdx-43b on /v1/generate; 2) enabled throughput-priority dynamic batching; 3) applied anonymous rate limit 200/min; 4) added enterprise override to keep low latency for premium keys; 5) CS notified for impacted customers.

maria (oncall): Handoff plan: I will remain active for another 30m then hand off to night oncall @tyler. Handoff notes: watch p95 and 5xxs, check per-pool queue length, revert changes if error rate rises or customer complaints spike. Rollback command:
```bash
# rollback batching window to default
redwoodctl runtime update --pool gen-usw2-1 --model rdx-43b --route /v1/generate \
  --set max_batch_latency_ms=20 --set max_batch_size=64 --set batching_strategy=latency-priority
```

tyler: Copy, I'll take it. Will monitor dashboards and escalate to infra if we see sustained >3% 5xx or p95 > 3s.

maria (oncall): Thanks team. I'll post a short incident summary in #inc-1769154321 and update status page if needed. We'll keep this incident open for now until metrics are stable for 1h.

jen: CS will follow up with affected customers and offer credits where appropriate.

alex: Metrics note for postmortem: correlate small-request keys with batch composition, consider automated per-key batching hints in future to avoid global tradeoffs.

maria (oncall): Agreed — add to postmortem action items. Closing active mitigation thread; monitoring-only now."
